claims.text: The newest published MCP specification revision is 2026-07-28.

evidence_passages.text: As of **2026-08-27**, the newest published MCP specification revision is **`2026-07-28`**.

claims.text: The immediately preceding revision to 2026-07-28 was 2025-11-25.

evidence_passages.text: This document lists changes made to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification since the previous revision, [2025-11-25](/specification/2025-11-25).

claims.text: Revision 2026-07-28 made MCP stateless by removing protocol-level sessions and the initialize/initialized handshake, and by moving protocol version and client capabilities onto each request.
acceptable_patterns: Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities

evidence_passages.text: Remove protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the Streamable HTTP transport. List endpoints (`tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`) no longer vary per-connection.

Make MCP stateless: remove the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake. Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`).
**Stateless Protocol Core**: MCP transformed from a bidirectional stateful protocol to a request/response stateless model.

claims.text: Revision 2026-07-28 added a mandatory server/discover RPC, and clients may use it as a backward-compatibility probe on STDIO.

evidence_passages.text: Add `server/discover`: servers MUST implement this RPC to advertise their supported protocol versions, capabilities, and identity. Clients MAY call it before any other request for up-front version selection, or use it as a backward-compatibility probe on STDIO.

claims.text: Revision 2026-07-28 introduced Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR) to replace server-initiated requests that needed held-open streams, enabling mid-call user confirmation or parameter collection over stateless protocols.

evidence_passages.text: **Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR)**: Replaces server-initiated requests that previously needed held-open streams, enabling mid-call user confirmation or parameter collection over stateless protocols.

claims.text: Revision 2026-07-28 replaced the HTTP GET endpoint and resources/subscribe and resources/unsubscribe with subscriptions/listen, a single long-lived POST-response stream for opted-in server-to-client change notifications.

evidence_passages.text: Replace the HTTP GET endpoint and `resources/subscribe`/`resources/unsubscribe` with `subscriptions/listen`: a single long-lived POST-response stream for opted-in server-to-client change notifications.

claims.text: Revision 2026-07-28 added caching metadata so list responses now include ttlMs and cacheScope.

evidence_passages.text: **Caching Support**: List responses now include `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` parameters for improved client-side caching strategies.

rejected_claims.text: The stateless core is the single biggest or most important change for local tool servers.
rejected_claims.reason: The supplied evidence labels this ordering as inference or judgment, not an official or directly supported ranking.

rejected_claims.text: Header-based routing is less important for stdio-only local servers because stdio has no header layer.
rejected_claims.reason: The evidence separately mentions header-based routing and describes stdio transport, but the comparative importance judgment is not directly supported.

rejected_claims.text: No newer specification revision exists after 2026-07-28.
rejected_claims.reason: The evidence supports that 2026-07-28 is current as of 2026-08-27, but the broader timeless claim is time-unstable.
